checks: No eclipse at 1 of 3 covered epochs where the 30.41527 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 94041900 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 30.415271 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 3.95 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The detection achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 80.1 in the initial analysis, with pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise of 8.3, though the centroid offset of 4.9 arcsec from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true period is twice the initial detection - a pattern flagged during automated quality checks. The machine-learning screening score of 0.65 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than a false positive.
